chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Al-Qassim ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Hazim narrated to us, saying: 'Ubays ibn Hisham an-Nashiri narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Jiblah, from Fudayl al-Sa'igh, from Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Thaqafi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:
When the people lose sight of the Imam, they will remain for years not knowing which one is which, then Allah will make their Master appear to them.

key_terms.أَيًّا مِنْ أَيٍّ: Which one is which (referring to distinguishing the true Imam from pretenders)
key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: The Imam, specifically the Twelfth Imam in this context
key_terms.صَاحِبُنَا: Our Master/Owner, a title for the Imam

ai.seo_question: What happens to the Muslim community during the occultation of the Imam?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the prolonged period of the Major Occultation (al-Ghaybah al-Kubra), characterized by a state of confusion where people struggle to distinguish the true Imam from pretenders. It underscores the divine promise of eventual manifestation, reassuring the Shia community that despite the delay and uncertainty, Allah will ultimately reveal the rightful leader to establish justice.
